Virat Kohli.bio: Former Indian captain across all formats, modern master of run chases and one of the most prolific run-scorers in cricket history.

Rohit Sharma.bio: India captain, World Cup winning skipper, and the only player in ODI history with three double centuries including 264.

MS Dhoni.bio: Iconic Indian captain who won the 2007 T20 World Cup, 2011 ODI World Cup, and 2013 Champions Trophy with legendary finishing skills.

Sachin Tendulkar.bio: The 'God of Cricket' with 100 international centuries and over 34,000 international runs across a celebrated 24-year career.

Jasprit Bumrah.bio: World-class pace spearhead known for his lethal yorkers, deceptive slower balls, and unmatched control in all formats.

Shubman Gill.bio: Young batting sensation, stylish top-order opener, and double centurion in ODI cricket.

Ravindra Jadeja.bio: Elite 3D all-rounder celebrated for world-class fielding, pinpoint left-arm spin, and clutch lower-order batting.

Hardik Pandya.bio: Dynamic seam-bowling all-rounder with game-changing power hitting and crucial medium-pace bowling in white-ball cricket.

KL Rahul.bio: Technically gifted batter and reliable wicketkeeper who excels in multiple batting positions across formats.

Suryakumar Yadav.bio: T20 sensation known as 'Mr. 360' for his audacious stroke-play, inventive geometry, and match-winning strike rates.

Rishabh Pant.bio: Fearless counter-attacking batter and wicketkeeper known for historic match-winning fourth-innings knocks in Tests.

Mohammed Shami.bio: Premier seam bowler celebrated for an immaculate upright seam presentation, reverse swing, and World Cup wicket-taking feats.

Mohammed Siraj.bio: High-energy fast bowler known for hostility with the new ball, relentless stamina, and explosive spells in ODIs and Tests.

Shreyas Iyer.bio: Authoritative middle-order batter and captain, exceptional against spin bowling and a proven anchor in 50-over cricket.

Kuldeep Yadav.bio: Rare left-arm unorthodox wrist spinner with multiple international hat-tricks and deceptive drift and turn.

Axar Patel.bio: Accurate left-arm spinner and destructive lower-order batter who delivers crucial breakthroughs under pressure.

Yuzvendra Chahal.bio: Wily leg-spinner and former chess champion with unmatched tactical courage and the highest wickets for India in T20Is.

Shikhar Dhawan.bio: 'Gabbar' of Indian cricket, iconic left-handed opener with a legendary record in ICC multinational tournaments.

Suresh Raina.bio: The first Indian to score a century in all three formats, electrifying fielder, and linchpin of India's 2011 World Cup squad.

Yuvraj Singh.bio: Player of the Tournament in the 2011 World Cup, six sixes in an over in 2007, and one of cricket's ultimate match-winners.

Gautam Gambhir.bio: Steely top-order anchor who top-scored in both the 2007 T20 World Cup Final (75) and the 2011 World Cup Final (97).

Virender Sehwag.bio: Revolutionary attacking opener who scored two Test triple centuries and an ODI double century with uncomplicated boundary mastery.

Sourav Ganguly.bio: 'Dada' - charismatic captain who forged a fearless modern Indian cricket team and scored 11,000+ ODI runs as 'God of the Off-side'.

Rahul Dravid.bio: 'The Wall' of Indian cricket, one of the greatest Test batsmen with impenetrable defensive technique and 24,000+ international runs.

Anil Kumble.bio: India's leading wicket-taker of all time (619 Test wickets, 337 ODI wickets) and one of only three bowlers with a 10-wicket Test innings.

Zaheer Khan.bio: Master tactician of pace and reverse swing, India's leading wicket-taker in the triumphant 2011 World Cup campaign.

Harbhajan Singh.bio: 'Turbanator' - fiery off-spinner with over 700 international wickets, including India's first Test hat-trick in 2001.

Kapil Dev.bio: India's iconic 1983 World Cup-winning captain, legendary fast-bowling all-rounder with 434 Test wickets and 5,000+ runs.

Ishant Sharma.bio: Towering pace bowler with 100+ Test caps, relentless workhorse length, and over 300 Test wickets for India.

Bhuvneshwar Kumar.bio: Supreme swing bowler with legendary control over conventional and reverse swing in powerplays and death overs.

Ravichandran Ashwin.bio: Spin maestro and cerebral cricketer with 500+ Test wickets and 5 Test centuries, master of carrom balls and flight.

Ajinkya Rahane.bio: Dependable overseas Test specialist and calm captain who led India to the historic Border-Gavaskar Trophy victory in 2021.

Yashasvi Jaiswal.bio: Prodigious young opening batsman known for fearless strokeplay, Test double centuries, and rapid-fire T20 innings.

Sanju Samson.bio: Gifted wicketkeeper-batter celebrated for effortless power hitting, aesthetic timing, and T20 international centuries.

Cheteshwar Pujara.bio: The modern 'Wall' of Indian Test cricket, celebrated for epic batting vigils and pivotal overseas series wins in Australia.

Mayank Agarwal.bio: Solid opening batter with multiple Test double centuries, known for dominating spinners with aggressive footwork.

Washington Sundar.bio: Composed all-rounder who bowls economical powerplay off-spin and delivers match-winning middle-order batting.

Shardul Thakur.bio: 'Lord Shardul' - a golden-arm strike bowler known for partnership-breaking spells and blistering counter-attacking fifties.

Deepak Chahar.bio: New-ball swing specialist who holds the record for the best bowling figures in T20I history (6 for 7 vs Bangladesh).

Rahul Chahar.bio: Attacking leg-spinner with quick arm speed, sharp googlies, and a proven track record in high-pressure T20 tournaments.

Ravi Bishnoi.bio: Fast-skidding leg-spinner with a vicious, hard-to-pick googly who climbed to the No. 1 ICC T20I bowling ranking.

Arshdeep Singh.bio: Clutch left-arm pace bowler, World Cup champion, and master of pinpoint yorkers and deceptive cutters in death overs.

Umran Malik.bio: 'Jammu Express' - one of the fastest bowlers India has produced, consistently clocking 150+ km/h with fiery bouncers.

Avesh Khan.bio: Hit-the-deck pace bowler with sharp pace, heavy back-of-a-length deliveries, and disciplined death-over execution.

Prasidh Krishna.bio: Tall hit-the-deck fast bowler who extracts steep bounce and sharp seam movement from good length areas.

Mukesh Kumar.bio: Accurate line-and-length seam bowler known for relentless accuracy, swing with the new ball, and dependable death bowling.

Shivam Dube.bio: Towering left-handed power hitter celebrated for towering sixes against spinners and handy medium-pace bowling.

Rinku Singh.bio: Ice-cool finisher celebrated for hitting five consecutive sixes in a final over and mastering high-pressure chases.

Tilak Varma.bio: Composed left-handed stroke player with exceptional maturity, fluent square-wicket hitting, and calm temperament.

Jitesh Sharma.bio: Hard-hitting middle-order wicketkeeper-batter known for innovative 360-degree boundary striking from ball one.

Ruturaj Gaikwad.bio: Classy, technically pristine top-order batter and captain, IPL Orange Cap winner with effortless lofted drives.

Devdutt Padikkal.bio: Tall and elegant left-handed opener with graceful cover drives and strong domestic and Test performances.

Venkatesh Iyer.bio: Versatile seam-bowling all-rounder with aggressive opening batting style and handy medium-pace wicket-taking ability.

Nitish Rana.bio: Combative left-handed batter and handy off-spin bowler with extensive leadership and middle-order match-winning knocks.

Rahul Tripathi.bio: High-intent batter who attacks from ball one, celebrated for selfless strokeplay and fast scoring in powerplays.

Dinesh Karthik.bio: Long-serving Indian wicketkeeper celebrated for iconic last-ball six in Nidahas Trophy and elite T20 death finishing.

Robin Uthappa.bio: Attacking opener with a trademark 'walking down the pitch' shot, 2007 T20 World Cup winner and IPL Orange Cap champion.

Ambati Rayudu.bio: Gritty middle-order anchor with a fearless mentality, six-time IPL champion and reliable ODI run-scorer for India.

Kedar Jadhav.bio: Unorthodox round-arm spinner and handy middle-order batter known for breaking crucial partnerships unexpectedly.

Manish Pandey.bio: The first Indian to score an IPL century, outstanding outfielder and clutch run-chase specialist in white-ball cricket.

Murali Vijay.bio: Classical Test opener with magnificent leaves outside off-stump, key contributor to India's overseas Test successes.

Parthiv Patel.bio: Diminutive wicketkeeper-batter who made his Test debut at age 17, known for aggressive opening batting in powerplays.

Wriddhiman Saha.bio: Acclaimed as one of India's finest pure glovemen against spin and pace, with centuries against Australia and West Indies.

Karun Nair.bio: Only the second Indian cricketer after Virender Sehwag to score a Test triple century (303* vs England in Chennai).

Stuart Binny.bio: Medium-pace all-rounder who holds India's best-ever bowling figures in ODIs (6 wickets for 4 runs vs Bangladesh).

Mohit Sharma.bio: Smart seam bowler celebrated for deceptive back-of-the-hand slower balls and IPL Purple Cap-winning death bowling.

Varun Aaron.bio: Genuinely rapid pace bowler who consistently exceeded 150 km/h with aggressive bouncers and express pace.

Umesh Yadav.bio: Out-and-out fast bowler with lethal reverse swing, skiddy trajectory, and formidable home Test bowling averages.

Jaydev Unadkat.bio: Experienced left-arm pacer, domestic stalwart who led Saurashtra to multiple Ranji Trophy titles with swing and cutters.

Navdeep Saini.bio: Athletic fast bowler capable of bowling upwards of 145+ km/h with high seam action and venomous yorkers.

T Natarajan.bio: 'Yorker King' from Tamil Nadu who bowled toe-crushing yorkers in all three formats during the historic 2020-21 Australia tour.

Khaleel Ahmed.bio: Tall left-arm pace bowler with natural angle away from right-handers and wicket-taking ability in powerplays.

Sandeep Sharma.bio: Master of conventional swing bowling with the ability to swing the ball prodigiously both ways inside powerplays.

Piyush Chawla.bio: World Cup winning leg-spinner (2007 T20, 2011 ODI) with a deadly googly and one of the highest wicket-takers in T20 history.

Amit Mishra.bio: Traditional classical leg-spinner with big-turning leg-breaks, flight, and the only bowler with three IPL hat-tricks.

Pragyan Ojha.bio: Accurate left-arm spinner who won Player of the Match in Sachin Tendulkar's farewell Test with 10 wickets.

RP Singh.bio: Key architect of India's 2007 T20 World Cup triumph, lethal left-arm swing bowler with devastating late inswing.

Munaf Patel.bio: Unsung hero of India's 2011 World Cup-winning team, renowned for disciplined length and reverse-swing bowling.

S Sreesanth.bio: Fiery swing bowler with an upright seam, famous for taking the catch that won the 2007 T20 World Cup final.

Irfan Pathan.bio: Prodigious swing bowler who took a historic first-over Test hat-trick against Pakistan and won Player of the Match in 2007 T20 WC Final.

Yusuf Pathan.bio: Towering destructive power-hitter, two-time World Cup winner (2007 T20, 2011 ODI) who turned matches with brutal boundaries.

Ashish Nehra.bio: Resilient left-arm fast bowler famous for his historic 6 for 23 against England in the 2003 World Cup.

VVS Laxman.bio: 'Very Very Special' - majestic wristy stylist whose 281 against Australia at Eden Gardens is regarded as one of cricket's greatest innings.

Javagal Srinath.bio: India's premier pace spearhead of the 1990s, taking over 550 international wickets with genuine pace and bounce.

Venkatesh Prasad.bio: Master of seam movement and deceptive leg-cutters, famously clean-bowling Aamer Sohail in the 1996 World Cup quarter-final.

Mohammad Azharuddin.bio: Long-serving Indian captain and wristy strokeplayer who started his career with three consecutive Test centuries.

Ravi Shastri.bio: Champion of Champions in 1985 World Championship, gritty all-rounder and historic head coach who led India to glory in Australia.

Sunil Gavaskar.bio: 'Little Master' - the first batsman to score 10,000 Test runs, legendary opener with immaculate technique against unhelmeted pace.

Dilip Vengsarkar.bio: 'Colonel' - stylish middle-order batter with an imperious drive who scored three consecutive Test centuries at Lord's Cricket Ground.

Gundappa Viswanath.bio: One of India's finest batsmen against pace and spin, master of the square cut; India never lost a Test in which he scored a century.

Mohinder Amarnath.bio: 'Jimmy' - Player of the Match in both the semi-final and final of India's triumphant 1983 World Cup campaign with courageous batting.

Syed Kirmani.bio: World-class wicketkeeper who won Best Wicketkeeper award in the 1983 World Cup with agile glovework to India's spin and seam attack.

Madan Lal.bio: Tenacious all-rounder who took the vital wickets of Viv Richards and Desmond Haynes in the 1983 World Cup Final.

Roger Binny.bio: Leading wicket-taker in the 1983 World Cup (18 wickets), devastating swing bowler in English conditions and BCCI President.

Sandeep Patil.bio: Swashbuckling middle-order batter known for hitting Bob Willis for six boundaries in an over and crucial half-century in 1983 semi-final.

Krishnamachari Srikkanth.bio: Pioneering attacking opener who top-scored with 38 in the low-scoring 1983 World Cup final against the mighty West Indies.

Ajay Jadeja.bio: Dynamic ODI finisher and brilliant fielder, famously smashing 45 off 25 balls against Waqar Younis in the 1996 World Cup quarter-final.

Vinod Kambli.bio: Flamboyant left-handed batsman who scored back-to-back Test double centuries and shared historic 664-run school partnership with Tendulkar.

Nayan Mongia.bio: Reliable wicketkeeper with sharp glovework to Kumble and Harbhajan, scoring an opening Test century against Australia in Delhi.

Manoj Tiwary.bio: Prolific domestic run-machine and ODI centurion for India, domestic captain who led Bengal cricket for over a decade.
